title: Postal Service Mail Carriers
description: Sort and deliver mail for the United States Postal Service (USPS). Deliver mail on established route by vehicle or on foot. Includes postal service mail carriers employed by USPS contractors.

tasks.text: Return to the post office with mail collected from homes, businesses, and public mailboxes.
Register, certify, and insure parcels and letters.
Sign for cash-on-delivery and registered mail before leaving the post office.
Hold mail for customers who are away from delivery locations.
Return incorrectly addressed mail to senders.
Maintain accurate records of deliveries.
Record address changes and redirect mail for those addresses.
Complete forms that notify publishers of address changes.
Deliver mail to residences and business establishments along specified routes by walking or driving, using a combination of satchels, carts, cars, and small trucks.
Meet schedules for the collection and return of mail.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Leave notices telling patrons where to collect mail that could not be delivered.
Provide customers with change of address cards and other forms.
Scan labels on letters or parcels to confirm receipt.
Obtain signed receipts for registered, certified, and insured mail, collect associated charges, and complete any necessary paperwork.
Sort mail for delivery, arranging it in delivery sequence.
Turn in money and receipts collected along mail routes.
Bundle mail in preparation for delivery or transportation to relay boxes.
Travel to post offices to pick up the mail for routes or pick up mail from postal relay boxes.
Answer customers' questions about postal services and regulations.
Sell stamps and money orders.
Report any unusual circumstances concerning mail delivery, including the condition of street letter boxes.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Address Management System AMS, Automated Data Collection System ADCS, End of Run Report EOR.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Delivery operations information system DOIS.

skills.name: Map creation software
skills.def: Software to place data or metadata on a map. May include surveying or engineering features. Examples: Delivery Routing System DRS.
